summary: Yuba County lookout: a 1913 tree platform, then a 1961 cab and tower from Lexington Hill moved here in 1983; listed as standing, and detecting fires in 2019 per NHLR.

facts.design: National Plan CL-100 cab (13x13 cabin) on a 20-foot steel tower, moved here from Lexington Hill

staffing.status: usually staffed during fire season (per 2006 photo caption)

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Plumas National Forest

events.note: Watchman spent the summer in the tree station; fires reported by telephone to the main office at Nevada City
Platform built around a large pine, nearly 80 feet up, because no funds were available for a tower
Lookout from the Pike County station first discovered a fire in Camptonville
Joseph Shaffer opened the station on May 14
Fire near Forbestown reported from the lookout in August; destruction limited to one acre
Mrs. J. W. Vance served as lookout with her four-year-old son as companion
Night shift placed on the lookout after fires were found to be set at night
On Lexington Hill, the 1933 structure's tower was replaced by a CL-100 cab on a 20-foot steel tower; this unit was later moved to Pike County Peak
Cab and 20-foot steel tower dismantled on Lexington Hill and re-erected on Pike County Peak
Registered October 30, 2019 as US 1374, CA 197; nominated by Brad Eells
Register says the lookout was actively detecting fires in 2019

corrections.proposed: Relocated 1983; cab and tower built 1961 on Lexington Hill
corrections.why: The NHLR Built field reads 'Relocated 1983'. Firetower.org dates the CL-100 cab and 20-foot tower to a 1961 replacement on Lexington Hill; 1983 is when they were moved to this site.

The Register describes a 20 foot steel tower. The roughly 80 foot figure (24.4 m) matches the 1913 tree platform, not the current structure. 6.1 m is tower height only; the cab adds height that no source gives.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 3,443 ft (1,049 m); Peakbagging gives 3690 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure of 1,049.4 m.
The 1913 tree platform, the 1923 permanent structure and the 1961 Lexington Hill cab are separate stages. Read together they do not conflict.

notes_for_editor: Brief errors: built 1983 is the relocation year, and height_m 24.4 m is the 1913 tree platform (see corrections). No source read gives visitor access or climbing rules, so the story says so and no access key is set. Staffing evidence is a 2006 photo caption plus 1920s-40s newspaper items; no current staffing data was found. One WebSearch was used.
